source_notes.label: Water-to-surfactant ratio and particle size
source_notes.summary: The source compares unannealed w = 3 and w = 5 powders and reports mean TEM sizes of4.5 and7.4nm, respectively. It attributes the larger size to greater water/AOT ratio. Exact w = 3 precursor and water charges are missing, so the result is not converted into a complete alternative charge recipe.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 2–3, Figures3–4 and size discussion

source_notes.label: Washing removes residual surfactant
source_notes.summary: For one comparison batch, elemental C/H falls from9.26/1.69wt% after one toluene wash to3.93/0.72wt% after toluene/methanol washing. FTIR supports removal of AOT. The typical preparation instead uses repeated sonication with toluene, ethanol and hexane, followed by TOP treatment; those sequences remain distinct. C/H is not a quantitative ligand coverage.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 2, Washing discussion and Figure1

source_notes.label: Feed mode changes elemental composition
source_notes.summary: Two dropwise reactions yield elemental-analysis ratios Bi1.00Te0.95 andBi1.00Te1.10, distinct from the intended Bi2Te3 composition. Their water/AOT ratios, exact feed quantities and structures are unreported. They do not inherit the microscopy or phase figures of the rapid-addition powders.

source_notes.label: Annealing and diffraction
source_notes.summary: Annealing w = 5 powder at230°C for4h underHe sharpens its diffraction peaks. Both unannealed and annealed patterns agree with commercial Bi2Te3 reference powder. No annealed particle-size number or refined atom coordinates are supplied.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 2, Figure2 and XRD discussion

source_notes.label: Small TEM counts limit the conclusion
source_notes.summary: Agglomeration prevents an accurate particle-size distribution. The reported means use21particles forw = 3 and28forw = 5, with estimated mean-size uncertainty strictly<10%. This is not a polydispersity value or normal-distribution standard deviation.

source_notes.label: Thermoelectric motivation remains future work
source_notes.summary: The introduction discusses quantum-confinement predictions and earlier thermoelectric systems. The present paper supplies synthesis, elemental analysis, diffraction and microscopy; measuring quantum-confinement effects on thermoelectric properties is left to future work. No current Seebeck coefficient, conductivity or thermoelectric figure of merit is assigned.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 1,3, Introduction and Summary

source_notes.label: Air handling and external oxidation evidence
source_notes.summary: Presence-versus-absence-of-air experiments show no observable differences at the reported stage. The oxidation/XPS observation is attributed to external reference17, not a current-study XPS panel or evidence of indefinite air stability.

evidence_conflicts.summary: Source Figure1 prints Wavelength(cm−1), retained without silent correction.
Mean uncertainty<10% is distinct from an unmeasured distribution width.
